purpose: Metoprolol is used to treat high blood pressure, chest pain (angina), and heart failure. It is also used after a heart attack to help protect the heart and improve survival. Sometimes doctors prescribe it to help control an irregular or fast heartbeat.
how_it_works: Your heart has special receptors that respond to stress hormones like adrenaline, which can make your heart beat faster and harder. Metoprolol blocks those receptors, so your heart slows down a bit and does not have to work as hard. Think of it like putting your heart in a calmer, more relaxed mode.
common_side_effects: Feeling tired or sluggish, dizziness, slow heartbeat, cold hands or feet, upset stomach, and sometimes mild shortness of breath. Most of these tend to improve after your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor first — stopping abruptly can cause a dangerous rebound effect, including chest pain or heart attack. Tell your doctor if you have asthma or breathing problems, diabetes, or liver disease. This medicine can also mask some signs of low blood sugar if you are diabetic, so monitor your blood sugar closely.
typical_dosing: Doses vary depending on what it is being used for. A common starting dose for high blood pressure is 25 to 100 mg once or twice a day. The long-acting version (Toprol-XL) is usually taken once a day. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, and try to take it at the same time each day.
